# Kome.Reconcile known-answer vectors. tests/test_reconcile.adb reads them.
# SIMPLIFY.md S11, S18, S19; AUDIT.md H12 (the ceil of a HELLO); all integers
# big-endian:
#   data key      = 03 || ent[16] || sub:u8 (0 DEL, 1 PUT) || fh[32] || h[32]  (82 B)
#   auth key      = tag || 0^17 || signer[32] || h[32]  (tag 0 ROSTER, 1 REVOKE, 2 GRANT)
#   prologue      = "kome/1" || ns (= cid[0:16]) || proto (01)
#   HELLO         = 01 || n_auth:u32 || n_data:u32 || digest[32] || cred_len:u16
#                   || ceil_len:u16 || cred || ceil  (45 + cred_len + ceil_len B,
#                   at most 17 877)
#   ROOT          = 05 || count:u48 || fp[32]
#   RANGE         = 02 || k:u8 || bounds[k+1] x key[82] || k x (count:u48 || fp[32])
#   ELEMENTS/HAVE = 03/04 || lo[82] || hi[82] || n:u16 || n x (flen:u16 || frame)
# Provenance: an independent Python reference made these vectors from the
# layouts above (the frames and credentials are opaque bytes here; each
# item frame starts with its element key, as the test's frames do). The
# script is at the end of this file, on the "#|" lines. It prints
# everything above them, with this command:
#   sed -n 's/^#| \{0,1\}//p' reconcile.txt | python3 -I -
# Filler: fill(n, s)[i] = (s + 7 i) mod 256.
# Formats:
#   dkey     <ent> <del|put> <fh> <h> <key, hex>
#   akey     <tag> <signer> <h> <key, hex>
#   prologue <cid> <wire, hex>
#   hello    <n_auth> <n_data> <digest> <cred, hex, or -> <ceil, hex, or -> <wire, hex>
#   root     <count> <fp> <wire, hex>
#   range    <k> <bounds concatenated> <counts, comma-separated> <fps concatenated> <wire, hex>
#   elements <tag> <lo> <hi> <frames, comma-separated hex, or -> <wire, hex>
